examples: Keep a plain shell in a tab next to the agent you are working with.
Keep a review board in a tab next to the agent that is working on it, and split it out beside the terminal.
Keep the Task Manager list in a tab beside the agent that is working on it.
how_to: Press the + at the end of a terminal's tab strip.
Pick an agent, a terminal, a blueprint or the browser; it opens as a tab beside the terminal.
Or drag a session from the agents drawer onto a terminal's tab strip to add it there as a tab.
A tab shows a small cyan workflow icon right of its title while that session has a workflow running.

Pick browser in the + menu for a new proxy browser, or any page, file or browser already open (a review board is a page); it opens as a tab. Drag a row from the sidebar's browsers, files or review list onto a strip, a pane edge or the middle of a pane to do the same. A plain click on one of those rows still takes over the main area.

Pick widget in the + menu to open any widget (notes, tasks, files...) as a tab beside your terminals; it wears the widget's icon, title and alert badge, and a right-click on it (or its icon) opens the widget's own menu, including the selected session | all sessions switch and close tab. A tab you are not looking at fetches nothing. Widget tabs open on a larger screen; the phone strip shows sessions only.

Right-click a tab (or focus it and press the Menu key or Shift+F10) for that session's menu, drawn in the tab's own theme. In the kebab on the strip's right, actions folds out beside the menu, which stays open.

name: Terminal component tabs
summary: open another agent, a terminal, a blueprint, a browser, an open page, an open file or any widget as a tab alongside your terminal, and right-click any tab for its menu.
where: The + (new tab) at the end of a terminal's tab strip, on the terminal page.
